summary: This article explains how a camera lets in reflected light, focuses it with a lens, times it with a shutter, and records it on film or a sensor.
introduce: Read the title “How Cameras Capture Light” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: to bounce back light, heat, or sound
the opening that lets light into a camera
a thin strip with chemicals on it that changes when light hits it, used in old cameras

challengeTerms.def: to bend light as it passes from one material into another
the amount of time light is allowed to reach a camera's film or sensor

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that taking a good photo depends more on light than on the camera? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Compare a camera and the human eye.
struggling: Pre-teach reflect, aperture, and film with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use refract, inverted, and exposure in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
